the following issues:
  1. The generation of the BAU within the framework of the SU(2)⊗SU(2)⊕U(1) model, with a first-order phase transition in the scalar sector.
the generation of the Baryon Asymmetry of the Universe ( BAU ) in the context of the Left-Right Symmetric Model (LRSM).

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the baryon number violation and the CP violation are two sides of the same coin, in a unified theory.
the BAU is generated in a natural way within the framework of the SU(2) _{L} ⊗ SU( 2 ) _{R} ⊗ U( 1 ) models.
the baryon asymmetry of the Universe is a natural prediction of the left-right symmetric models.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can generate a BAU in the range 10 −9 − 10 −10 at the weak scale, for the case of the first-order phase transition.
, within the left-right models, the observed value of the baryonic assymetry of our Universe can be obtained from CP violating processes, at the scale of the electroweak interactions.
the baryon asymmetry of the Universe is generated at the scale of the weak interaction, and the observed value is related to CP-violating parameters of K 0 − ¯ K 0 mixing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the BAU can be generated in the early Universe, even if the sphaleron rate is very low.
the baryon asymmetry of the Universe can be produced at the weak scale, without the need of a large CP violation in the neutrino sector, and without the need of new sources of CP violation.

the observed value of BAU can be explained by the scattering of the Standard Model (SM) particles off the first-order electroweak phase transition (EWPT) bubbles, in a left-right symmetric extension of the Standard Model, with an additional Higgs doublet.
